meta.frame_definition: Chassis-plate-local frame (matches hardware/src/config.py conventions): origin xy = chassis plate center; +X = robot right (FR leg has +X per config.HIPS); +Y = robot front; +Z = up. z=0 is the chassis PLATE BOTTOM face (i.e. world_z - zb, where zb = body_h + HIP_DROP is the plate-bottom world height used throughout tools/make_visuals.py). This makes all positions here independent of body_h / leg stance height, matching the task note that the pod is non-movable relative to the chassis. To get world Z for a given body_h: world_z = pos_mm[2] + body_h + config.HIP_DROP.
meta.method_summary: (1) Each candidate small kit part STL was loaded, bbox-centered, scaled x1.5 (project convention, see tools/make_head_eyecut.py / config.py). (2) Cabin_Front_Blue and Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired were processed identically, then scanned for sharp dihedral-angle edges (face_adjacency_angles, thresholds 8-34deg swept) whose connected vertex components form circular or rectangular boundary loops (technique established in earlier sessions for the Head_Top eye sockets, see project memory 'tachikoma-design-pitfalls' #24). (3) Loop diameters/footprints were matched against each part's own measured cap/base dimensions, expecting a ~1.05-1.15x socket oversize margin (the ratio observed for the already-confirmed Head_Top eye socket: 42.3/37.7=1.122). (4) Local-axis-to-robot-axis mapping for each shell was derived analytically from the shell_ghosts rotation matrices (Front: local +Z -> robot +Y, local +Y -> robot +Z, local +X -> robot -X; Back: local +Z -> robot -Y, local +Y -> robot +Z, local +X -> robot +X) and confirmed against occlusion-correct 6-axis parallel-projection ray-cast renders. (5) Final candidate positions were cross-checked visually against /private/tmp/.../scratchpad/3mf_thumbs/thumbnail_middle.png (photo of the assembled painted kit) and a 2x zoomed crop of the pod region.

scratchpad/rear_pod/Cabin_Front_Blue_raycast6.png, Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired_raycast6.png (occlusion-correct 6-axis depth scans, generated this session)
meta.confidence_scale: high = clean single-cluster ring match with expected oversize ratio + position corroborated by photo; medium/medium-high = good size match but some position or aspect-ratio ambiguity; low/unresolved = could not be pinned down by this method, flagged UNVERIFIED with reasoning.
methodology_caveats_2026_07_28: source_offset (the 3MF-forensics method used so effectively for the front/head JSON, see kit_assembly_front.json method_summary) does NOT extend to this file's Cabin_Front_Blue/Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired absolute placement. All 119 3MF part-objects were re-scanned this session: only Cabin_Front_Blue.stl_A carries source_object_id=1 -- every other part in the ENTIRE kit (all 118 remaining objects, including Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired and every small Cabin_* trim part) carries source_object_id=0. source_offset is only additive within a single source_object_id's coordinate system, so Cabin_Front_Blue's own offset=(0,0,0) is NOT in the same coordinate system as any other part's offset (front or otherwise) -- substituting it in the same way that worked for e.g. Leg_Thigh_Guard/Leg_Thigh_Grey (both object_id=0, 0.00mm touching) produces physically-impossible results here (tried this session: Cabin_Eye_White landed at z=185-272mm, more than the whole shell's own 73mm height). CONSEQUENCE: this file's shell_ghosts()-derived absolute placement for Cabin_Front_Blue/Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired (rot(180,z)@rot(90,x) @ (0,-156,zb+55) / rot(90,x) @ (0,-235,zb+55)) is NOT independently re-confirmable from source_offset with the current 3MF metadata -- it remains the pre-existing, ring-extraction/photo-cross-checked 'reasoned' placement (see shell_reverification below, which validates internal Front/Back seam fit, not absolute world position).

A second, independent attempt was made to cross-check the Head vs Cabin absolute relationship (both are object_id=0, so source_offset SHOULD apply across them) using the already-forensically-validated Head_Bottom_Blue anchor (0.00mm-gap-verified in kit_assembly_front.json) to back-solve Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired's 'true' kit-space position. Result: (0, 11.7, -16.6) -- this places the Cabin pod almost exactly ON TOP of / inside the Head (whose own anchor is t=(0,12,-3)), which is physically impossible (a robot can't have its back-pod occupying the same space as its head). CONCLUSION: the original combined 3MF assembly evidently laid out the Head/Cabin/Leg/Arm kit clusters in separate, non-overlapping TRAY regions for print-plate/modeling convenience, not in their final assembled robot pose -- so source_offset substitution across sub-assembly cluster boundaries (Head<->Cabin, and by extension Cabin<->Leg/Arm) is NOT valid, even though it IS valid within a single cluster (e.g. Head_Bottom<->Head_Top<->Head_Plate, or Cabin_Front<->its own small trim parts once a Front-local anchor is independently established). Any future session attempting to re-derive Cabin's absolute chassis-plate position from source_offset should expect this same failure mode and needs a different anchor (e.g. a measured photo/physical relationship between Head and Cabin, not a 3MF coordinate substitution).

Print-quantity parts (any '_x2'/'_x4' name -- Cabin_RedLight_Large/Small_x4, Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey_x4, Cabin_Turret_Peg_x2, Cabin_Front_Insert_Back_Black_x2, Cabin_Front_Insert_Bottom_Long_Black_x2, Cabin_Peg_x2) only ever carry ONE recorded source_offset in the 3MF, even though the print-plate contains multiple copy-objects for them -- BambuStudio evidently records the same source coordinate for every duplicate instance of a given part. This means source_offset can identify WHICH single one of the N real installed positions a part's offset corresponds to (e.g. distinguishing 'front pair' vs 'back pair' for a part mounted on both Cabin_Front_Blue and Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired), but can NEVER by itself give all N positions -- the other N-1 instances still require the existing ring-extraction + photo-symmetry method (mirror/rotate the one resolved instance). See the Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey back-pair note for a worked (low-confidence) example of using this to sanity-check an existing front/back assignment.
methodology_caveats_2026_07_29: TURRET ORIENTATION FIX (user-reported '90-degree, sticking in perpendicular instead of lying flat'): confirmed and root-caused. TWO independent bugs compounded: (a) kit_assembly.py's rear-JSON rendering aligned each part's local +Z axis to outward_normal by default, but Cabin_Turrent_Left/Right_Grey's own true mounting-flange-normal (measured via sharp-edge ring extraction + largest-flat-facet cross-check on the raw STL) is ~102deg away from local +Z -- so the wrong local axis was being aligned. (b) the previously recorded outward_normal for BOTH turret entries equals the cabin-local (UNROTATED) ring normal used directly, without applying the Front shell's own ghost rotation (rot(180,'z')@rot(90,'x')) -- i.e. it was accidentally left in the wrong coordinate frame. Fixed by adding an explicit 'matrix' field per turret entry (kit_assembly.py now supports this for rear-JSON entries too, matching the convention already used in kit_assembly_front.json for Head_Eye_White_x3) that solves R from the CORRECTLY-measured flange normal and t so the flange centroid (not the STL's bbox center, which sits 8.58mm scaled away from the true flange center) lands exactly on the independently re-measured cabin socket ring center. Verified: 0.000mm centroid residual, 0.00deg normal residual (both solved-for by construction), and a whole-mesh interpenetration check (trimesh.contains on 3000 surface samples of the transformed turret vs the transformed Cabin_Front_Blue solid) shows mean penetration depth 0.001mm / max 0.004mm -- i.e. the flange sits flush to the curved hull surface within the mesh's own numerical noise floor.

SAME-CLASS BUG FOUND MORE WIDELY: re-deriving the outward_normal for Cabin_Eye_White and the Cabin_RedLight_Large front pair from scratch (independent sharp-edge ring extraction on Cabin_Front_Blue.stl, contains()-verified outward sign, properly shell-rotated) turned up normals differing from the prior session's recorded values by 13.8deg (Eye) and ~80.8deg (RedLight_Large front pair -- essentially a Y/Z swap, i.e. the SAME 'forgot to apply the shell rotation' bug as the turret, reproduced almost exactly: old RedLight outward_normal (0,0.08,0.997) equals the raw cabin-local ring normal verbatim). All entries carrying an outward_normal field were re-measured and corrected this session using one consistent, contains()-validated method (see per-entry 'method'/'finding' notes): Cabin_Eye_White, Cabin_Turrent_Left/Right_Grey, Cabin_RedLight_Large (all 4 instances), Cabin_RedLight_Small (all 4 instances, outward_normal ADDED where previously absent), Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey (all 4 instances, outward_normal ADDED). All 12 non-turret re-measured rings landed on a strikingly consistent panel-local outward direction (Front shell: local raw ~(0,0.08,0.997); Back shell: mirrored sign) -- a strong internal cross-check that these are genuine, correctly-identified mounting rings and not noise.

LOCAL-AXIS (Y vs Z) BUG found on Cabin_RedLight_Large/Small and Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey: trimesh.section() sampling along each part's own raw-STL length shows RedLight_Large/Small are plain right-circular cylinders (constant cross-section, X=Z=cap-diameter) with their true axis on local Y, and Spinnarette_Grey is a TAPERED shaft (cross-section area shrinks monotonically from root at -Y to a point tip at +Y) also on local Y -- i.e. the code's default local-+Z-to-outward_normal convention was wrong for all three part types (it would mount them lying roughly tangent to the hull surface instead of sticking out perpendicular-ish, the OPPOSITE symptom from the turret's bug but the same root cause: wrong local axis assumed). Fixed generically in tools/kit_assembly.py via a new LOCAL_AXIS_OVERRIDE dict (generalizes the pre-existing NORMAL_FLIP_PARTS mechanism used for Cabin_Eye_White) rather than per-entry matrices, since these parts' own bbox centers are already at/near their geometric axis (no large centroid-vs-tip offset like the turret's asymmetric dome).

NOT resolved this session (no completed-kit photo was available in this session's scratchpad -- the path referenced in project memory, .../scratchpad/3mf_thumbs/thumbnail_middle.png, did not exist when this session started and could not be regenerated without the original 3MF/photo source): (1) turret roll/barrel-yaw around the flange-normal axis -- trimesh.geometry.align_vectors() picks a deterministic minimal-angle rotation, which is geometrically valid (flange flush + 0.1mm/1deg thresholds met) but its 'clocking' (which way the nozzle silhouette points) was not cross-checked against a photo; a candidate secondary keying feature (~8.7mm round hole found on both the turret mesh and the cabin near the ring) was tested and RULED OUT as a valid correspondence (local vector angles 164.9deg vs 21.0deg between the two frames -- inconsistent, not a real feature pair). (2) Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey front/back assignment remains the existing 2026-07-28 'informational caution' (print-quantity part, source_offset can only anchor one of 4 instances) -- unchanged, not newly resolved. (3) bbox-center-vs-attachment-point offset for Cabin_Eye_White/RedLight_Large/RedLight_Small/Spinnarette_Grey (each part's own local mount-axis HALF-extent, raw*1.5 scaled, symmetric bbox so root-side and tip-side bounds are equal even for the tapered Spinnarette: Eye (Z axis) 7.39mm, RedLight_Large (Y axis) 2.94mm, RedLight_Small (Y axis) 2.94mm, Spinnarette (Y axis) 8.19mm -- these bound how far the true contact face sits from pos_mm along the mount axis, since oriented_mesh() places each part's bbox center, not its contact face, at pos_mm) was NOT solved exactly (would need each part's own counterbore/socket depth, not available) -- reported as a bounded UNVERIFIED residual per part, see the calling session's residual table.

Cabin_Front_Insert_* (rect/slot parts) were NOT re-derived this session (ring-extraction is a circular-loop method; a quick attempt to find Cabin_Front_Insert_Front_Black's known 43.9x7.0mm rect slot via the same connected-component search did not converge on a clean candidate within a reasonable search radius, and a full rectangular-loop detector was out of scope for this session's time budget). A shape-only spot-check found Cabin_Front_Insert_Front_Black and Cabin_Front_Insert_Back_Black have their own thinnest raw-STL extent on local Y (not Z) -- same category of axis concern as RedLight/Spinnarette -- while Left/Right/Bottom_Long/Bottom_Wide are already thinnest on Z (consistent with the code's default, for whatever it's worth given none of the latter four currently carry any outward_normal / rotation at all). Left as-is (existing pre-2026-07-29 pos_mm, no rotation change) -- UNVERIFIED, flagged for a future dedicated rectangular-slot forensics pass.
methodology_caveats_2026_07_30: CABIN_BACK UPSIDE-DOWN FIX (user-reported, this session): the shell_ghosts()/pod_dress_shells() rotation for Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired, rot(90,'x') alone, was confirmed to be vertically inverted (dome-top/skirt-bottom sense flipped relative to the already-correct Cabin_Front_Blue) and corrected to rot(180,'y')@rot(90,'x'). IMPORTANT CAVEAT reconfirmed: the shell_reverification below (0.08mm Front/Back seam gap, 0cm3 boolean overlap) is UNCHANGED by this fix and does NOT by itself distinguish the two orientations -- both Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired's raw-STL bounding box (X range [-47.261,47.261], Y range [-60.839,60.839], Z range [-15.910,15.910], all symmetric about the local origin to 5+ significant figures) and the seam-gap metric are invariant under this fix, because a 90-degree-multiple rotation of an origin-symmetric bbox only permutes/flips axis signs, never changes the bbox itself or the resulting world Y-extent used for the seam check. This is exactly the pitfall flagged in project memory 'tachikoma-design-pitfalls' -- seam/ring-fit metrics cannot detect a 180-degree flip of a quasi-symmetric shell; only asymmetric features + photo cross-check can.

EVIDENCE 1 (raw-mesh cross-section asymmetry, calibrated against the already-correct Front shell): both Cabin_Front_Blue and Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired have a genuinely asymmetric local-Y profile (local Y is confirmed the shells' shared 'vertical' axis -- both old and new rotations map it to world Z, and it is each mesh's largest raw extent, 130.1mm/121.7mm respectively, consistent with the dome-to-skirt height). Sampling X/Z cross-section span in 20 bins along local Y: Front tapers to a narrow point at local Y=+65.0 (xspan 42.3mm, zspan 29.7mm -- this is the small knob/apex visible at the very top of the pod dome in scratchpad/3mf_thumbs/cabin_crop_big.png) and is widest (xspan 113.5mm) near local Y=-40, close to its Y=-65.0 flared-skirt edge (xspan 83.0mm at the very edge) -- i.e. narrow=dome-top, wide=skirt-bottom, and Front's CONFIRMED-correct rotation maps local Y=+65 (narrow) to world +Z (top). Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired shows the SAME shape of asymmetry: narrow at local Y=-60.8 (xspan 52.1mm, zspan 14.3mm) vs wide at local Y=+60.8 (xspan 79.7mm, zspan 26.9mm, with the widest point xspan 94.5mm around local Y=+27). Under the OLD rotation rot(90,'x'), local Y=-60.8 (the NARROW/dome-like end) mapped to world Z=-36.3 (the BOTTOM of the Back shell's world range) and local Y=+60.8 (WIDE/skirt-like end) mapped to world Z=+146.3 (the TOP) -- i.e. narrow=bottom, wide=top, the OPPOSITE pattern from Front. Under the NEW rotation rot(180,'y')@rot(90,'x'), local Y=-60.8 (narrow) maps to world Z=+146.3 (top) and local Y=+60.8 (wide) maps to world Z=-36.3 (bottom), matching Front's narrow-top/wide-bottom pattern.

EVIDENCE 2 (independent, from the already-measured back-mounted trim parts): Cabin_RedLight_Large/Small and Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey each have a front pair (on Cabin_Front_Blue, orientation not in question) and a back pair (on Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired). Under the OLD Back rotation, the recorded world Z heights were badly mismatched between the front/back pairs of the SAME part: RedLight_Large front Z=+109.98/+109.96 vs back (old) Z=-1.95/-1.30 (delta ~112mm); Spinnarette front Z=-28.15/-27.78 vs back (old) Z=+141.88/+141.53 (delta ~170mm, and note the SIGN of the mismatch is opposite RedLight's -- exactly what a vertical flip predicts, since it swaps which end of the shell each part lands near). Algebraically re-deriving each back-pair position/normal under the NEW rotation (exact: local = R_old^T @ (pos_old - t), pos_new = R_new @ local + t, i.e. the physical ring position on the mesh is unchanged, only the coordinate frame it is expressed in) gives RedLight_Large back Z=+111.95/+111.30 (front pair +109.98/+109.96, delta ~2mm) and Spinnarette back Z=-31.88/-31.53 (front pair -28.15/-27.78, delta ~4mm) -- i.e. the front/back pairs now land within a few mm of each other, consistent with a design that mounts the same trim part at matching heights on both shell halves. This is strong independent confirmation of the same fix EVIDENCE 1 derived from the shell's own geometry.

X-SIGN CONSEQUENCE: the fix rot(180,'y')@rot(90,'x') = (world 180deg flip about the Y/front-back axis) applied on top of the old rot(90,'x') necessarily flips both world Z (up/down, intended) and world X (left/right) -- this is forced by orthonormality once outward_normal (local Z -> world -Y, i.e. the shell's outward/backward-facing sign, contains()-verified in 2026-07-29's re-measurement and NOT reopened this session) is held fixed and local Y's world-Z sign is flipped: a proper rotation can only flip an even number of the three axis signs. CONSEQUENCE: for all 6 back-mounted trim-part instances (Cabin_RedLight_Large#back_left/right, Cabin_RedLight_Small#back_left/right, Cabin_Spinnarette_Grey#back_left/right), the recomputed X sign is opposite the old one, so the physical ring that was labelled '...#back_left' under the old (wrong) rotation is now on the ROBOT'S RIGHT, and vice versa -- the left/right key suffixes and 'side' fields were swapped accordingly (the underlying per-instance ring measurements, i.e. which diameter/method-text belongs to which physical ring on the mesh, were NOT altered, only which world position + which side label they resolve to).

translation_robot_z0 for Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired, (0,-235,55), is UNCHANGED by this fix and does not need re-deriving: the raw STL's own bbox is already centered at its local origin on all 3 axes to 5+ significant figures (X [-47.261,47.261], Y [-60.839,60.839], Z [-15.910,15.910]), so for any 90-degree-multiple axis rotation (which only permutes/negates coordinates) the transformed bbox's world center is exactly t regardless of which such rotation is chosen -- verified numerically this session (old and new rotations give byte-identical world bounding boxes for Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired, [Y:-258.865..-211.135, Z:-36.259..146.259] at zb=0).

NOT re-checked this session (out of the stated scope of 'Cabin_Back orientation + its own attached decoration'): Cabin_Peg_x2 (pos_mm still null/UNVERIFIED, unaffected since it is X-centerline-only and the seam Y-plane did not move); Cabin_Turrent_Left/Right_Grey, Cabin_Turret_Peg_x2, Cabin_Eye_White, and the Front-mounted RedLight/Spinnarette/Insert instances (all shell_mount=Cabin_Front_Blue, not Cabin_Back_Blue_Repaired, untouched); Head_TailJoint_Blue/Ball (shell_mount=pod_neck per their own entries, not the Cabin shell, untouched).

Cabin_Eye_White.method: 2026-07-29 RE-MEASURED (turret/rear-decor re-audit): re-ran the sharp-edge ring extraction on Cabin_Front_Blue.stl directly (face_adjacency_angles>15deg, SVD plane fit), found the same ring (n=64, dia=41.2mm, stdR=0.0008mm raw -- essentially a perfect circle) at cabin-local raw (0.0035,-40.813,32.104). Outward sign resolved by sampling +-eps along the candidate normal and checking trimesh.contains() against the watertight Cabin_Front_Blue solid (unambiguous: +normal direction is outside the solid at eps=2..15mm). Transformed through the Front shell's own verified ghost transform (rot(180,'z')@rot(90,'x'), t=(0,-156,55) in robot z0 frame) to get pos_mm/outward_normal above.
Cabin_Eye_White.finding: SUPERSEDES the prior pos_mm/outward_normal (0,-111.5,-7.5 / 0,0.99,-0.16). Root cause of the prior error: the previous session's outward_normal does not match either the raw cabin-local ring normal (0.0001,0.0801,0.9968) OR the correctly-shell-rotated version -- it appears to have been derived from a noisier/different ring candidate or partial rotation. Position delta from the old value: (−0.005,+3.66,+1.28)mm (old was off-ring by ~2.6mm on the cabin's own local frame). Angle delta on outward_normal: ~13.8deg (old (0,0.99,-0.16) vs new (0,0.997,0.080) -- exceeds the 1deg re-audit threshold, corrected here). Position residual after fix: ~0.00mm to the ring centroid used as target (ring itself is stdR=0.0008mm raw = 0.0012mm scaled, i.e. sub-0.01mm circularity). NOT fixed this round: bbox-center-vs-visible-tip offset (Cabin_Eye_White's own local Z half-extent is 4.93mm raw = 7.39mm scaled -- oriented_mesh() places the part's bbox center, not its visible-tip apex, at pos_mm, so the actual visible dome apex sits ~7.4mm further out than pos_mm and the wide gluing rim ~7.4mm further in; resolving this exactly would need the eye's own internal socket-depth, not attempted this session -- bounded UNVERIFIED depth residual, see residual table).

Cabin_Turrent_Left_Grey.method: 2026-07-29 REPLACED (turret 90-degree-orientation fix, user-reported): the part's TRUE mounting-flange plane was found on the raw Cabin_Turrent_Left_Grey.stl itself via sharp-edge ring extraction + largest-flat-facet cross-check (both agree to <0.5deg): a clean circular flange, local raw centroid (-5.215,2.327,-0.376), local raw outward normal (-0.9591,0.1865,-0.2128) [trimesh facet-normal convention, i.e. pointing away from the turret's own solid material], dia 22.6-23.2mm raw = 33.9-34.8mm scaled (close to the prior session's 35.67mm claim; small method variance). This flange axis is ~102deg away from the part's local +Z -- NOT close to it -- so the generic rear-JSON convention (align local +Z to outward_normal) put the turret ~90-100deg off, i.e. mounted with the flange roughly PERPENDICULAR to the hull instead of flush/parallel, matching the user's exact complaint ('90度誤り...垂直に刺さっている'). The matching socket on Cabin_Front_Blue was independently re-measured (not reused from the prior session): a near-perfect circular ring (n=64, stdR=0.0007mm raw, dia 40.6mm scaled -- matches the prior '40.3-40.6mm' note) at cabin-local raw (43.345,17.928,-5.457). Outward sign resolved via trimesh.contains() point-sampling (unambiguous). ROOT CAUSE of the prior outward_normal=(0.95,0.23,0.19) also found: it equals the UNROTATED cabin-local ring normal (0.959,0.227,0.169) used directly as if it were already robot-frame -- the Front shell's own ghost rotation rot(180,'z')@rot(90,'x') (which maps local(x,y,z)->robot(-x,z,y)) was never applied. Corrected outward_normal above IS the properly shell-rotated value. Because the turret's own bbox-center (raw STL is pre-centered at origin) sits 5.72mm (raw) = 8.58mm (scaled) away from its true flange centroid, a rotation-only fix would still mis-place the part by that much -- so this entry now carries an explicit 'matrix' (SCALE baked into the 3x3 block, applied directly to raw vertices, same convention as kit_assembly_front.json's Head_Eye_White_x3) solving simultaneously for R (flange-normal to socket-normal, single-vector align_vectors -- roll/clocking about that axis is NOT independently constrained by any secondary feature found on this mesh; see residual table) and t (so the flange centroid lands exactly on the socket centroid, not the bbox center).
Cabin_Turrent_Left_Grey.verification: Flange-centroid-to-socket-centroid residual: 0.000mm (solved exactly by construction, unchanged by the 2026-07-29-B roll fix below). Flange-normal-to-socket-normal residual: ~0.03deg (was 0.00deg; the tiny nonzero value is floating-point noise from the original matrix's 6-decimal-place rounding, re-verified this session -- not a new physical gap). Whole-part interpenetration check (3000 surface samples vs the transformed Cabin_Front_Blue solid via trimesh.contains), re-run after the roll fix: 9.1% of samples nominally 'inside' with mean penetration depth 0.0009mm / max 0.0034mm -- essentially unchanged from the pre-roll-fix 9.0%/0.001mm/0.004mm, confirming the roll-only rotation (about the flange-normal axis) did not disturb the flush-mount fit. pos_mm/outward_normal above are the flange-centroid/socket values for documentation; the 'matrix' field is authoritative for rendering (kit_assembly.py oriented_mesh()).
Cabin_Turrent_Left_Grey.note: 2026-07-29-B: photo-cross-checked (was UNVERIFIED). Reference: scratchpad/3mf_thumbs/turret_ref_zoom.png (zoomed crop of the completed, painted kit's left flank) shows a slender barrel-like protrusion from the grey cone, angled forward and down from horizontal by roughly 20-30deg (eyeballed). Re-measured the raw Cabin_Turrent_Left_Grey.stl directly for this feature (independent of the flange work above): a single straight round shaft (~4.5mm raw dia, i.e. ~6.75mm scaled) runs through the dome roughly tangent to the flange plane (dot product with the flange normal = 0.0002, i.e. perpendicular to within noise) with local raw axis (0.1908,0.9816,0.0) -- found via PCA on the two symmetric end-cap vertex clusters (y<-17.22 / y>17.22 in the raw mesh, n=288 each), cross-checked against the tip-to-tip vector (agreement to 0.007deg). NOTE: this shaft passes essentially straight through the dome and is symmetric end-to-end (same ~4.5mm cap diameter both ends, both ends stand equally proud of the dome's own bulk) -- there is no secondary distinguishing feature that identifies one end as 'the barrel' vs a 'cone-center mounting stub' from the geometry alone, so this is functionally a single rod feature whose AXIS (not a specific end) was aligned to the photo target; because the fix is a pure roll about the flange-normal axis, both ends necessarily move together and the rendered mesh is identical regardless of which end is conceptually labeled 'barrel'. Previously (align_vectors default) this axis mapped to robot-frame (0.1735,0.9848,0.0006) -- i.e. dead horizontal (0.03deg from flat) and, per the prior note, not cross-checked -- matching the reported bug symptom (rod reads as horizontal / front-back symmetric in renders).
